result.title: A Constructive Orbit-Based Theory of Learnability
result.summary: We develop a finite-dimensional orbit framework for constructing data-adapted dictionaries, sparse realizations, and predictive extensions. The method uses wrapped weighted shifts to generate orbit dictionaries and local interpolation maps from independent orbit representatives, turning the learning problem into three explicit tasks: scaffold discovery, sparse realization on the discovered dictionary, and prediction through learned sparse coordinates. We introduce CCDS as the main constructive ingredient: a deviation-controlled sparse realization procedure that recovers MP/OMP-type behavior at the minimal-deviation boundary while allowing feasible interior paths with prescribed residual geometry that is inaccessible to MP/OMP. We prove generic orbit independence, exact block interpolation with norm control, observable bounds on sparse approximation distortion, sparse realization guarantees on selected supports, and fixed-path stability under admissible perturbations of the block interpolants. These results connect sparse approximation, interpolation, and finite-dimensional operator dynamics through the construction and analysis of data-induced orbit dictionaries. Experiments on synthetic geometry, controlled realization tests, and standard classification benchmarks show that selected orbit scaffolds have substantially better matched-rank projection behavior than random orbit or unstructured alternatives, that CCDS attains near-zero realization error at the minimal-deviation boundary, and that predictors trained from the sparse CCDS certificates give competitive performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出有限维「orbit」框架：用 wrapped weighted shift 构造数据自适应的字典与块插值映射，把学习分解为支架发现、稀疏实现与基于稀疏坐标的预测三步，并证明 orbit 独立性、插值范数控制、稀疏近似偏差界与扰动稳定性，配以合成与分类实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「稀疏实现偏差界」与块插值扰动下的路径稳定性，可能为刻画 latent 状态压缩中的信息损失与推理轨迹稳定性提供可核查的分析视角；是否可迁移仍待判断。
